context: This batch exists only to produce gate evidence for review step 5. It is NOT the T1 main experiment, it trains no model, and it changes no production semantics.

Two experiments are compiled, each a strict 2-cell paired design over ONE declared factor: execution.compute_delay_s (control 0.0 vs cd05 0.05). Trace identity, seed, endpoints, PHY and every other field are shared; the compiler enforces this via controlled_signature equality across the pair.

the micro experiment (this revision: EXP-20260923-T1-STEP5-MICRO-R06): 8 satellites / 1 plane real Walker geometry, demand.mode=csv with an explicit 6-row table (CODE/data/traffic/t1_step5_micro_ab.csv): one warm-up packet at t=0 and a 5-packet burst at t=3.00..3.20, 8e6 bits each, A=(0.1N,0.1E) -> B=(52.6N,90.4E), isl_rate 10 Mbps, uplink/downlink 1000 Mbps, control plane on (vis_k=2), routing hop, available_capacity_interval_s=0.1.

The micro experiment is NOT a reproduction of the #212 micro-mechanism fixture. That fixture uses tests/helpers.py StaticGeometry (a scripted 4-cycle plus an isolated satellite with a scripted visibility predicate). No formal config can express scripted geometry: kernel.py:1065-1071 falls back to model.Constellation (real Walker-delta) when no geometry object is injected, and the formal CLI never injects one. This batch therefore reuses ONLY the fixture's ROW TABLE SHAPE (warm-up + burst emission schedule, 8e6-bit packets) and its PHY/control parameters, on the known-good reachable site pair taken from the t1_pressure_corridor profile. No #212 or M1/M2/M3 mechanism conclusion may be drawn from this batch.

the 24-satellite corridor experiment (this revision: EXP-20260923-T1-STEP5-PRESSURE-R06): the EXISTING 24-satellite ISL pressure corridor. Its common_config is field-for-field identical to CODE/leo_sim/profiles/t1_pressure_corridor.yaml (profile file sha256 60bcb666160e72159018feaf2f93c7f2f01888cc06cd4655c04ed5b5aab2dc4e), which is a config file rather than a named profile (config.py:410 registers only 'smoke'). Equivalence is machine-checked, not asserted: load_config_file(profile) and resolve_config(inlined common_config) both resolve to config_sha256 52dfe3d92c1e0e6cbd7281c8b4725d9889c5c2376848a22a5b25a980ed4c47a3, and that value equals the compiled control-arm config_sha256. No 280-satellite scenario was created.

execution.available_capacity_interval_s is non-null in BOTH experiments (1.0 for the corridor, 0.1 for the micro). This is required: the independent recomputation reports DEGENERATE_DENOMINATOR with utilization=None when no availability sample exists, and a degenerate group must not be used as gate evidence. The corridor profile comment at CODE/leo_sim/profiles/t1_pressure_corridor.yaml:69-73 states the same requirement.

Neither request declares execution_policy, so the v2_serial_gate predecessor gate is a documented no-op (v2_serial_gate.py:52-55) and the two cells of each experiment may be launched independently. This is a deliberate, disclosed design choice: the batch measures static recomputation agreement, not a serial ordering effect.

KNOWN PLATFORM LIMITATION that the reviewers must assess: a formal authorized run CANNOT carry a decision audit log. __main__.py:332-335 refuses --decision-log when the run is formal ('decision audit log is diagnostic-only and cannot be attached to a formal authorized run'), and remote_job.formal_command (remote_job.py:303-310) never passes it, so decision_sink is None and ledgers.json (receipt.py:544-556) contains no decision rows. The task's original witness ('decision_sink rows with t > t_decision_start') is therefore NOT obtainable from formal artifacts. The substitute witness is a deterministic local non-formal diagnostic re-execution of the SAME resolved config with --decision-log, which is only admissible if it is proven to be the same execution as the formal run (identical trace_sha256 AND bit-identical packet_events/link_service_windows digests). If that proof fails for any cell, the decision-count witness must be reported as unavailable for that cell and no substitute may be used.

Both experiments use real Walker geometry and are therefore descriptive of this platform's mechanics only; the corridor retains the profile's ACCESS_QUEUE_OVERFLOW behaviour, which is a real property of the existing profile and not a defect introduced here.

NEW IN R04, EXTENDED IN R05 - mechanical executable-procedure gate (tools/check_procedure.py, inside the reviewed artifact set). This is the positive fix for the defect class found in all three review rounds: a process document treated as executable while nothing mechanically compared it to the tools it invokes. G1: no run command may reference another revision, and the documented run commands must be exactly this revision compiled cells (config path, authorization path, session). G2: the declared primary_metric must actually be accepted by the toolchain, proven by invoking the same dispatch the RUNBOOK-mandated analyzer uses, not by reading code. G3 (phase all): the documented chain must reach the launcher accept/reject decision point, by running the exact module run-remote.sh invokes plus the exact authorization-binding check the launcher performs, for every cell. G4: the gate and the procedure must themselves be in the reviewed artifact set. Any failure means REVISE and no formal run.

PLATFORM-LEVEL DEFECT REGISTERED SEPARATELY (raised for the initiator, deliberately NOT mixed into this batch conclusions and NOT repaired here): this is the SECOND time that adding one config key invalidated every compiled manifest and every existing authorization - the first was execution.compute_delay_s, this one execution.node_process_delay_s. At merge time there is NO mechanical guard that can tell, before the merge, that existing compiled planned-run rows and authorizations will all become unverifiable. Candidate fixes: (a) snapshot the resolved-key set of a representative config and fail CI on any change to it, so a schema change is forced to declare its blast radius; (b) make manifest/authorization verification attribute the failure explicitly (for example new-config-key-invalidates-existing-bindings) instead of a generic cells do not derive from request, so the cause is legible at the point of failure.

FINDING RECORDED (self-discovered, not hidden): the FIRST version of gate check G1a used the regex EXP-[A-Za-z0-9_]*-R(dd), which forbids hyphens. Real ids look like EXP-20260923-T1-STEP5-MICRO-R06, so the scan matched NOTHING and G1a passed VACUOUSLY - the very failure mode this gate exists to prevent. Measured before the fix: real ids seen = [] (vacuous pass). After the fix (hyphens allowed) both real ids are seen, and the mandatory negative control detects an injected EXP-20260923-T1-STEP5-MICRO-R99 as foreign. The defect was found and fixed by the producer before review was requested.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS ARE MANDATORY IN EVERY CHECK (hard requirement from the initiator). check_procedure.py runs a negative control inside every check and prints its result: G1a injects a foreign revision id; G1b corrupts one documented session and requires a mismatch; G2 probes an unsupported metric name and requires REJECTION; G3 probes a wrong run id and requires REJECTION; G4 checks a synthetic artifact set with a zeroed gate hash and requires a reported problem. A check whose control does NOT trigger is reported as an UNPROVEN GATE, listed in unproven_gates, and is NOT counted as passed: all_checks_ok is true only when no executed check failed AND none is unproven. Checks that cannot run yet (G3 before an authorization exists) are listed in skipped_checks and are not counted as passed either.

REVISION 5 RESPONSES to the R04 adversarial BLOCK, each verifiable by running the gate. (1) G1 is no longer fence-scoped: G1a scans the entire document text for experiment ids and its mandatory negative control injects a foreign id into UNFENCED text; G1b additionally fails loud on any command-like run-remote.sh line that is not inside a fenced block matching a compiled cell, with a control that injects exactly such an unfenced invocation. The producer reproduced the R04 defeat (fenced-only scan missed an unfenced stale id) and confirmed the new whole-document scan catches it. (2) All stale hash and revision claims are swept; the corridor equivalence value is the F2-era 52dfe3d92c1e0e6cbd7281c8b4725d9889c5c2376848a22a5b25a980ed4c47a3. (3) The F2 disclosure is now mechanically backed by gate check G5, which reads each cell resolved execution.node_process_delay_s, reports the actual value in the gate report, and has a control proving the predicate flags a non-zero value.

GATE CHECKS IN REVISION 5 (all with executed negative controls, all printed every run): G1a foreign revision id anywhere in the document; G1b run-remote invocations match compiled cells AND are fenced; G2 declared primary_metric accepted by the analyzer dispatch; G3 (phase all) the chain reaches the launcher accept/reject decision point; G4 the gate and procedure are inside the reviewed artifact set; G5 F2 is disabled with the actual resolved value reported. A check whose control does not trigger is an UNPROVEN GATE, listed in unproven_gates, and is NOT counted as passed.

STRUCTURAL FIX (revision 6, initiated as option A after three evaded scanning patches). The gate no longer scans prose. tools/procedure_commands.py is a reviewed artifact that DERIVES the four formal run commands from the compiled run-manifests, and gate check G0 requires R06/PROCEDURE.md to contain the derived marked block byte-for-byte between GENERATED-RUN-COMMANDS markers. Deviation of any kind - fenced, unfenced, line-split, re-cased, variable-assembled, or edited by one character - is not the generated text and fails G0. This is the structural guarantee, and the report names it explicitly.

G0 NEGATIVE CONTROLS, required to trigger on every run (otherwise G0 is an UNPROVEN GATE and cannot count as passed): a single-character mutation inside the generated block must be detected, and removing the two marker lines from the document must be detected. Both are printed in the gate report. An end-to-end check was also performed by the producer: editing exactly one byte of the generated block in the real procedure file (offset 9719, character 6 to 7) made the gate exit 1 with G0 failed; the file was then restored byte-identically (sha256 e936b2db32d836982f68507536cdb7aa49ea88ff7005095aabe6376ee2fca317) and the gate returned green.

SCOPE OF THE GUARANTEE, stated plainly so reviewers can judge it: G0 guarantees that the commands printed in the procedure are exactly the commands derived from the compiled manifests. It does not and cannot guarantee anything about other prose in the document. G1a and G1b remain only as hygiene checks for realistic accidental drift and are known to be evadable by line-splitting and re-casing; they are labelled HYGIENE in the gate report and must not be cited as the structural guarantee.

The evidence chain is unchanged and must not be re-litigated: the compiled cells, the paired design (shared trace_identity_sha256 and controlled_signature, differing config_sha256), the corridor profile equivalence, the F2-disabled evidence (gate check G5 reports the actual per-cell value), the harness self-test and the registered chain-2 blind spot with its three mandatory backstops all carry over from revision 5 unchanged.
